  <div class="ws-instruction">
    One row per planned wave. Wave 0 is tasks with no dependencies; the ordering is directional and strict. For each wave name the
    committed output it builds on, set the parallel agent count using the trade-off table beside B3, state the scope boundary, and
    write the checkpoint as an observable behavior, the command that observes it and the output expected. Checkpoints are authored
    properly in <b>WS-CS-APM-checkpoint-assertions</b>; transcribe them here.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>B3 decision aid &mdash; the wave-sizing trade-off table <span class="ws-block-note">ch18 L163&ndash;172 &middot; observed, one input among four</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup><col style="width:16%"><col style="width:42%"><col style="width:42%"></colgroup>
      <thead><tr><th>Factor</th><th>Smaller waves (2-4 agents)</th><th>Larger waves (6-10 agents)</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td class="prior">Execution time</td><td class="prior">3-5 minutes</td><td class="prior">8-12 minutes (slowest agent dominates)</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="prior">Debug difficulty</td><td class="prior">Low &mdash; few changes to inspect</td><td class="prior">High &mdash; more changes interacting</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="prior">Commit granularity</td><td class="prior">Fine &mdash; easy to bisect</td><td class="prior">Coarse &mdash; harder to isolate regressions</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="prior">Overhead</td><td class="prior">Higher &mdash; more validation cycles</td><td class="prior">Lower &mdash; fewer cycles<span class="prior-src">ch18 L165&ndash;170</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
    <p style="font-size:7.6pt;margin:1.5mm 0 0"><b>Heuristic (ch18 L172):</b> start with smaller waves. Combine tasks into larger waves only when they are genuinely independent (different files, different concerns, no shared state) and when the validation overhead of extra cycles outweighs the debugging advantage.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-foot-quote">
    "The dependency is directional and strict: no task in wave N may depend on a task in wave N+1." (ch18 L142)
  </div>

      <h1>Wave Decomposition Plan and Self-Sufficiency Check</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">Part C is the task table &mdash; one block per wave, at the session granularity an agent actually receives. Print one sheet per epic.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-18-wave-decomposition-plan</b><br>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>Ch 18 &mdash; The Execution Meta-Process</b> L174&ndash;178 and L159 &middot; <code>handbook/ch18-the-execution-meta-process.qmd</code> &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch18-the-execution-meta-process.html#sec-meta-wave-decomposition">#sec-meta-wave-decomposition</a>

  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Take one real epic and work it task by task, wave <span style="display:inline-block;width:12mm;border-bottom:.25mm solid #93a0ad"></span>.
    Run the self-sufficiency test <b>aloud</b>, with the question worded exactly as printed, and have someone <b>other than the task's author</b>
    give the verdict. Authors say yes to their own tasks because the missing context is in their head. Anything not ready is refined, split, or moved to a later wave.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Part C &mdash; The task table <span class="ws-block-note">rows are tasks &middot; printed, one sheet per epic</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:5%"><col style="width:10%"><col style="width:10%"><col style="width:8%"><col style="width:9%"><col style="width:9%"><col style="width:17%"><col style="width:14%"><col style="width:9%"><col style="width:9%">
      </colgroup>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th><span class="fno">C1</span> Session / task number</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C2</span> The task, in one sentence</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C3</span> Key context to load</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C4</span> Single deliverable</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C5</span> Exclusive file list (feeds Part D)</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C6</span> Self-sufficiency verdict</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C7</span> If not ready, why</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C8</span> Action taken</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C9</span> Path whitelist enforced</th>
          <th><span class="fno">C10</span> Hand-off contract to the next session</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="prior">Shape from the worked five-session table<span class="prior-src">ch13 L509&ndash;523</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Worked instances are one line each, verb first, scope explicit.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L509&ndash;523</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Instruction file, prior session's output, external reference &mdash; three items, not twelve.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L509&ndash;523</span></td>
          <td class="prior">A file path or a named test suite &mdash; one per session.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L509&ndash;523</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Must not overlap another task in the same wave.<span class="prior-src">ch18 L159</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><i>can an agent complete this task without asking me a question?</i><span class="prior-src">ch18 L176</span></td>
          <td class="prior">The three named causes are the first three options.<span class="prior-src">ch18 L176</span></td>
          <td class="prior">The chapter's three permitted responses are the only options.<span class="prior-src">ch18 L176</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Worked instance: a session limited to two directories; the agent began extending into a third and the boundary stopped it. The suggestion went in its summary and was handled later by the agent with the right context.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L495&ndash;497, L525&ndash;529</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Worked instance: the downstream session received only the API contract &mdash; endpoint URLs, request and response shapes &mdash; not the implementation details.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L523</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text sm"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-box"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span><span class="f-text"></span><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-box"></span></td>

          <td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">ambiguous design decision</span><span class="opt">unclear scope</span><span class="opt">undocumented conventions in the target file</span><span class="opt">other</span></div><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">refine the instructions</span><span class="opt">split the task</span><span class="opt">move to a later wave</span></div></td>

    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch18-the-execution-meta-process.html#sec-meta-wave-decomposition">#sec-meta-wave-decomposition</a>
    &middot; resolutions: <code>ch17</code> L277, L279
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    <b>Build this part in a spreadsheet, or generate it with a script against the repository.</b> Sorting by file path is how D4 finds anything,
    and a printed table cannot be re-sorted. This page is the column layout and a short paper fallback for the first few paths. Every engineer
    whose files appear here must be in the room or have agreed ownership in advance; where two teams both claim a file, the named arbiter decides.
    Do not dispatch while any D4 reads yes.
  </div>

          <td class="prior">&mdash;<span class="prior-src">ch18 L159</span></td>
